messages:
maya: Heads-up — quickstart curl fails for me with a TLS cert error and then a billing 402 when I force it through.
maya: curl https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/firstcall -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -> x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
maya: if I use --insecure the response body is {"error":"workspace_pending_billing","message":"workspace needs billing setup"} but my Console shows a card on file.
kevin: two likely causes: (1) corporate proxy/CA causing the TLS error, and (2) the token might belong to a different org. run `curl -v` for the cert chain and `curl https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/whoami -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"` to confirm org.
maya: curl -v shows server cert subject CN=corp-proxy.local issuer CN=Corp Internal CA. whoami returns org_id: org_personal_81 but Console selected org is org_team_99. i pulled the wrong token from my password manager. sigh.
samir: that explains the 402. For the TLS, avoid --insecure in docs; recommend adding the internal CA to the OS trust store or set env vars: `export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/corp-ca.pem` (python) or `export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/corp-ca.pem` (node). quick temporary: `curl --cacert /path/to/corp-ca.pem https://...`.
maya: switched to the correct org token and set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE; quickstart completes now. thanks.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: CI job ci/quickstart-e2e for maya failed at 2149877000 due to TLS; auto-retry initiated.
devex-bot: doc suggestion: add a small "verify your token/org" step (whoami) as the first command in quickstart and a short note about corporate proxies. consider surfacing a clearer API error when token org != dashboard org.
kevin: agreed — i'll file a tiny docs PR with the whoami snippet and a one-paragraph proxy troubleshooting note. tag @samir for the CA instructions.
maya: PR opened and linked here. thanks all :sparkles:
